PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   B. Overload every socket
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun

2. When learning Oblique Projection, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Oblique Projection.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Oblique Projection.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Oblique Projection.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Oblique Projection.

3. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Keyboard
   B. CPU
   C. Speaker
   D. Monitor

4. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Input Cable Tester
   C. Information and Communication Technology
   D. Internal Cooking Timer

5. When learning Safety on Raised Platforms, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety on Raised Platforms.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Safety on Raised Platforms.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Safety on Raised Platforms.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Safety on Raised Platforms.

6. When learning Self- Exploration and Career Development, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Self- Exploration and Career Development.

   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Self- Exploration and Career Development.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Self- Exploration and Career Development.

7. When learning Visual Programming, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Visual Programming.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Visual Programming.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Visual Programming.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Visual Programming.

8. When learning Holding Tools 8 4.2 Driving Tools 8 4.3 Project 20 5.0 Entrepreneurship 5.1 Fina, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Holding Tools 8 4.2 Driving Tools 8 4.3 Project 20 5.0 Entrepreneurship 5.1 Fina.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Holding Tools 8 4.2 Driving Tools 8 4.3 Project 20 5.0 Entrepreneurship 5.1 Fina.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Holding Tools 8 4.2 Driving Tools 8 4.3 Project 20 5.0 Entrepreneurship 5.1 Fina.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Holding Tools 8 4.2 Driving Tools 8 4.3 Project 20 5.0 Entrepreneurship 5.1 Fina.

9. When learning Visual Programming 15 3.0 Materials for Production 3.1 Wood 8 3.2 Handling Waste, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Visual Programming 15 3.0 Materials for Production 3.1 Wood 8 3.2 Handling Waste.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Visual Programming 15 3.0 Materials for Production 3.1 Wood 8 3.2 Handling Waste.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Visual Programming 15 3.0 Materials for Production 3.1 Wood 8 3.2 Handling Waste.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Visual Programming 15 3.0 Materials for Production 3.1 Wood 8 3.2 Handling Waste.

10. When learning Driving Tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Driving Tools.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Driving Tools.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Driving Tools.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Driving Tools.

11. When learning Wood, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Wood.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Wood.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Wood.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Wood.

12. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Work alone with eyes closed
   B. Remove all guards
   C. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   D. Run with the tool

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Government and Business and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Business Plan 6 Total Number of Lessons 120 Note: The suggested number of lesson and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
